headline: Iran talks drag on and Americans head to the polls
summary: The week was dominated by talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the run-up to Tuesday's U.S. midterms, and Canada–U.S. trade and a weakening economy after the Bank of Canada's rate hike. In Ontario, Toronto re-elected Olivia Chow, the province's deficit grew to $16.9 billion, and a violent Bridle Path home invasion shook the city.

top.headline: Iran's two-day Hormuz plan waits on U.S. as Trump vows the war ends soon
top.what: Iran and Qatari mediators shortened a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to two days, but it depends on Washington, and Trump says the war will end soon one way or the other after pledging no strikes before Tuesday's vote.
top.why: Oil above US$110 is the main force behind higher inflation in Canada and the U.S., and it pushed the Bank of Canada into a rate hike this week.

top.headline: Carney widens trade push as U.S. deal stays out of reach
top.what: With a deal on U.S. tariffs still elusive, Prime Minister Mark Carney is stepping up trade talks with other partners, while a reshuffled list of Canadian goods facing 50% U.S. tariffs took effect Friday.
top.why: Ontario sells most of its steel and auto output to the U.S., and the province says steel exports there have fallen by more than half since 2024.

top.headline: Economy stalls in August, two days after Bank of Canada's hike
top.what: Statistics Canada says the economy was flat in August and probably shrank 0.1% in September, a weak backdrop for the Bank of Canada's first rate increase since 2023.
top.why: The data shows the bank raising rates into a stalling economy, a tough trade-off that makes its next moves less predictable.

top.headline: Ontario deficit grows to $16.9 billion; balance pushed to 2029-30
top.what: Finance Minister Peter Bethlenfalvy's fall update raised this year's deficit by more than $3 billion and delayed a balanced budget by a year as the trade war slows growth.
top.why: A bigger deficit and slower growth limit room for new programs and tax relief, and confirm the trade war is hurting Ontario more than other provinces.

top.headline: 53 million early votes as Trump closes in Iowa and Kansas
top.what: Early voting far outpaced 2022, and Democrats lead most recent polls in key Senate races heading into Tuesday.
top.why: A Democratic Congress could check Trump's tariffs and war powers, while Republican control would give him a freer hand for the next two years.

top.headline: U.S. economy grows 3.4% in third quarter as inflation cools
top.what: The U.S. economy expanded at a 3.4% annual rate from July to September, faster than the spring, while a key inflation gauge eased.

top.headline: Russian grid strikes continue as Kherson truce ends
top.what: Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid cut electricity to about 280,000 households, while a large drone attack hit an industrial site near a major Russian refinery.
top.why: Talks in early November could be the first real test of a ceasefire path since early this year.
